items.title: Dan Wall and Adam Nussbaum interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 19, 2001
items.q: for him to take me on the road, which he had never done before with a pianist

ctx.x: I think the biggest thrill is when your mentors tell you that they dig what you’re doing. That’s the greatest. You know like with the people you look up to who have kind of encouraged you, either directly or just through their divine inspiration, you know, come up to you and go yeah man, you’re playing your ass off, or you sound great, or yeah baby. That makes it all worth it.

I think something that made me feel, in a different way, it’s really in a different type of music, but it was a real like a nice feeling was I did some touring with Henry Mancini and where he’s in his own thing, what a legend. And to be on stage, I mean for him to take me on the road, which he had never done before with a pianist, but to take me on the road and then here I am with the orchestras with full orchestra on stage and hanging out with Henry and we’re laughing and we’re having fun, that was another kind…

Yeah I mean when people that you’ve really dug hire you and you get to play with some of your heroes, that’s the greatest feeling. I mean to play with people that you’ve listened to for years and have inspired you and then be on the bandstand with them, that’s like wow, what a great feeling. And sometimes you can’t believe it, you have to like pinch yourself how’d this happen? And well I’ve just got to take care of business, stay focused, the bandstand is holy territory, we’re all there together, trying to find…
